title: Grade 3 Maths — Thu, May 28
description: Fractions — Half, Quarter, Third — Day 4 of 5
subject: mathematics

questions.question: What fraction is 'one half'?
questions.explanation: One half = 1/2. When something is split into 2 equal parts, each part is one half.

questions.question: A pizza is cut into 4 equal pieces. You eat 1 piece. What fraction did you eat?
In the fraction 3/4, what does the '4' represent?
questions.explanation: The bottom number (denominator) shows how many equal parts the whole is divided into.

questions.question: Which fraction is the largest?
questions.explanation: 1/2 is the largest. When the top number (numerator) is the same, SMALLER denominator = LARGER fraction.

questions.question: If you colour 2 out of 3 equal parts of a shape, what fraction is coloured?
Which two fractions are EQUAL?
questions.explanation: 2/4 = 1/2. Both represent exactly half of something. They are equivalent fractions.

questions.question: A ribbon is 12 cm long. One third is red. How many cm is red?
How many quarters make a whole?
What fraction of the week is Saturday and Sunday?
questions.explanation: A week has 7 days. Saturday + Sunday = 2 days. 2 out of 7 = 2/7.

questions.question: Which fraction is the SMALLEST?
questions.explanation: 1/4 is the smallest. Larger denominator with numerator 1 = smaller fraction.

questions.question: Amara has 8 stickers. She gives half to her friend. How many does she keep?
What do you call the top number of a fraction?
questions.explanation: The top number is the numerator — it shows how many parts are taken.
